subject: Re: Encord/Signatrix - Path Forward
text:
Hi Leo,

Thank you for your note and for sharing more context. We truly want to work with you, as we clearly see the advantages of your solution and believe this can become a strong partnership.

As you know, we are now part of ITAB, a publicly listed Swedish company. Our internal processes and requirements unfortunately do not allow us to sign software license or SaaS agreements with long fixed terms.

If we can agree on a contract with a monthly termination option, we would be able to sign and start already in August. 
If the termination period is two or three months, I would need to take this back to ITAB’s CFO Office. As this position is currently vacant, no decision could be expected before the end of the year.

Please understand that we are also investing into this partnership, and ITAB itself is looking to expand further into AI and computer vision in the mid-term, which could also represent an interesting opportunity for you. If your solution performs as well as you promise, there will be no reason for us to terminate, so from our perspective the risk for you is low. Or did I missed something? 

I fully understand that, especially as a startup, you prefer long-term contracts. However, our internal policy today does not allow us to sign for more than three months. Convince us with quality, and we will be a long-term and loyal customer.

Please feel free to make a suggestion on how we could move forward. If this structure is not possible for you, no problem: then we will move ahead with another solution and not block each other's time. 

Best regards,
Daniel

subject: Re: Tess <> Roger (Head of Partnerships at Encord)
text:
Hi Roger,

Likewise, great to meet and chat with you! Apologies I couldn't get back to
you sooner as I was at a conference.

Thanks for putting together a partnership proposal so swiftly. I genuinely
appreciate the opportunity to explore a collaborative pilot and am aligned
with the spirit of mutual enablement and referral outlined in the document.

After reviewing the proposed outcomes and timeline, I believe the goal of
securing 3 qualified referrals within a 3-month period may be a bit
ambitious, particularly given the enablement ramp-up and the time required
to identify and nurture suitable opportunities with existing clients.
Additionally, trials and POCs with prospective clients often span 3–4
weeks, which can compress the referral window significantly.

To ensure a meaningful and sustainable pilot, I’d like to suggest extending
the timeframe to 6 months. This would allow both teams the space to fully
engage in enablement activities, co-develop targeted materials, and
cultivate high-quality referrals that are well-matched to Encord’s platform
capabilities.

We remain enthusiastic about the potential of this partnership and are
confident that a slightly extended pilot will yield stronger results and a
more accurate reflection of long-term collaboration potential.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

Best regards,

Tess Valbuena

subject: Encord - Technical, Legal and Cyber Deep Dive
text:
Hello!

After 2 demos from Encord showing us the capability of the platform, this is a technical, legal and cyber deep dive into the system.

https://encord.com/

The outcome of this call is to understand any technical, legal and cyber concerns that need to be addressed to determine if we go to a trial phase. The idea is to have this landed in Genepi for reuse across workstreams, starting with METS.

Encord, please provide the commercial model you use and invite anyone who may need to be in this call.

Sky/NBCU - some of you are optional for this call, for those not optional, please share RSVP asap. Please also invite anyone from your teams who I may have missed.

Any questions, just drop me an IM.

Dylan Turnley
